<research_package>

## Research question
Does Calloway-Sum's advantage over Pellam-Sum carry over to text domains other than news?

## Methods summary
Calloway-Sum is an abstractive summarizer that first plans a sequence of salient entities and then generates the summary conditioned on that plan. Pellam-Sum is an abstractive summarizer of the same size without the planning stage. Lead-3 (the first three sentences of the input) is a simple extractive reference.

## Experimental setup
Calloway-Sum and Pellam-Sum are trained, tuned and checkpoint-selected using only the Ravenmoor News corpus (210,000 article–summary pairs). In-domain evaluation uses the Ravenmoor News test split (2,000 articles). Held-out domain, never used for training, tuning or model selection: Lindqvist-Sci (scientific articles to abstracts), 1,000 test documents. Metric: ROUGE-L F1 (%), mean over 3 seeds; inputs longer than the 4,096-token context are truncated identically for both models.

## Experiments and comparisons
- `exp1`: In-domain evaluation (Ravenmoor News test split)
  - comparison `exp1/cmp1`: Calloway-Sum vs Pellam-Sum, ROUGE-L, in-domain
- `exp2`: Held-out-domain evaluation
  - comparison `exp2/cmp2`: Calloway-Sum vs Pellam-Sum, ROUGE-L, per held-out domain

## Results tables

sentences.text: On the held-out Lindqvist-Sci scientific-article domain, Calloway-Sum achieved a higher mean ROUGE-L F1 (36.4%) than Pellam-Sum (34.9%), indicating that its advantage over Pellam-Sum extends to this single scientific-article domain.

The observed advantage on Lindqvist-Sci (1.5 percentage points) is larger than the in-domain advantage on Ravenmoor News (1.2 percentage points), but no statistical test was reported, so the reliability of these differences is not established.

Both models showed higher mean ROUGE-L F1 than the Lead-3 extractive baseline on the held-out domain (31.7%), but these results are limited to a single scientific-article dataset and to the ROUGE-L metric, and no statistical tests support the observed differences.

On the held-out Lindqvist-Sci scientific-article domain, Calloway-Sum achieved a higher mean ROUGE-L F1 (36.4%) than Pellam-Sum (34.9%), indicating that its advantage over Pellam-Sum extends beyond the news domain.

The observed advantage on Lindqvist-Sci (1.5 percentage points) is smaller than the in-domain advantage on Ravenmoor News (1.2 percentage points), but no statistical test was reported, so the reliability of these differences is not established.
Both models outperformed the Lead-3 extractive baseline on the held-out domain (31.7%), but these results are limited to a single scientific-article dataset and to the ROUGE-L metric.
Calloway-Sum achieved a higher mean ROUGE-L F1 than Pellam-Sum on the held-out scientific domain (Lindqvist-Sci), 36.4% vs 34.9%.

This advantage was observed in both the in-domain news test set (41.8% vs 40.6%) and the held-out scientific domain, suggesting that Calloway-Sum's benefit carries over to at least one non-news domain.
Both models also outperformed the Lead-3 extractive baseline on the held-out scientific domain (36.4% and 34.9% vs 31.7%).
However, no statistical tests were reported, so these differences in means are not established as statistically significant.
